name: pike
why: A long-lived dynamic language from the Lysator lab with an unusual lineage and a dedicated, quietly eccentric community.

brief.what_it_is: Pike is a dynamic programming language with a syntax similar to Java and C, published on the official site pike.lysator.liu.se. It is run through a pike executable. The homepage says it is simple to learn, does not require long compilation passes, and has built-in data types meant for fast data manipulation. The site offers source code and binary downloads, release notes, a module and function reference, and a learning guide.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage pitches Pike as a language that is easy to pick up, avoids long compile cycles, and handles data quickly with powerful built-in types. The download page also traces it back to a lineage that starts with the µLPC language from 1994 to 1996.

commands_seen.context: Gentoo install route from the download page: installs the eselect repository tool so the Pike overlay can be added.
Gentoo install route: adds the Pike git overlay as a repository.
Gentoo install route: builds and installs Pike from the overlay.

brief.install_notes: The download page lists prebuilt binaries for the most recent release, usually for Linux x86, Linux ppc and Solaris sparc. Debian, Gentoo and Foresight also ship their own packages. Building from git needs an existing Pike install, because parts of the source are generated; the recommended bootstrap is to install a source package first. The homepage's download links include source code, release notes and all downloads.
brief.standout: Pike has a long, unusual lineage, tracing back through µLPC to 1994, and it is still developed in the open by a community that holds regular meet-ups and a conference at Roxen's Linköping offices. It is licensed under GPL, LGPL and MPL, so you can choose the terms that fit your project.
brief.status: Maintained. The homepage news shows a 9.0.13 beta on 2026-05-09, which is the fourth beta of the 9.0 series, plus a 9.0.11 beta on 2025-12-11. It also lists a 2026-Q3 meet-up on Aug 2 and a 2026 conference on Oct 31 and Nov 1. The download page refers to a development branch called 9.1 and a stable branch 8.0.
brief.caveats: The two pages disagree on the current version: the homepage points to 9.0.13 beta, while the download page says the latest stable is 8.0.1956. Binary builds are only said to be made for a few platforms, so other systems may need to build from source. Building from git requires an existing Pike install. The download page's 9.1 branch is described as a bleeding-edge development branch. The homepage calls the language a dynamic programming language but says nothing about a package manager or ecosystem. No module or function reference URL was captured, though the homepage links to one.
quotes: Pike is a dynamic programming language with a syntax similar to Java and C.
It is simple to learn, does not require long compilation passes and has powerful built-in data types allowing simple and really fast data manipulation.
Pike is free software, and is released under the GNU General Public License, GPL, GNU Lesser General Public License, LGPL and Mozilla Public License, MPL.
